why i support ending telework experiences like this show why its necessary this was for a direct hire authority i have the degree same grade level and job series as advertised and i am a step 3

as a federal employee ive always valued professionalism and transparency in our work environment however my recent experience with a hiring process has solidified my belief that telework policies while convenient for some can lead to severe lapses in accountability and responsiveness

in december i applied for a federal position and had legitimate concerns about my application status i emailed the designated staff member on december 17 2024 seeking clarification about my eligibility and qualifications to this day i have not received a response

the lack of communication and followup is not only unprofessional but likely caused me to miss out on a career opportunity its very possible the position was filled between december 17 and today leaving me with no recourse to address misunderstandings or appeal the decision

this lack of responsiveness is unacceptable when employees are working remotely it becomes easier for them to neglect essential duties avoid accountability and ignore critical emails in this case a potential opportunity was lost because of poor work ethics and an apparent lack of oversight

im not saying telework is inherently badmany federal employees work diligently and responsibly however for those who exploit it as an excuse to avoid their duties telework enables behavior that damages trust in the system

instances like this show why i agree with efforts to end telework or implement stricter accountability measures for remote workers the federal government owes its employees and the public the highest standards of professionalism situations like mine should never happen and they erode the trust and efficiency of our workforce

why banking sick leave is not silly and how teleworkremote work can fit in 

hi long time lurkerfirst time poster

bluf  my bottom line that i express with certainty and the associated sense of arrogance and please forgive this period of sometimes rambling is yes it is very very important to bank as much sick leave as you can because everything can change in a brief second  if you dont need it it is a nice thing to tack on six months to a year of service time to your retirement record  if you are trying to work out with your office a unique reason specific teleworkremote work model and they are balking feel free to give them a copy of this

i retired in june of 2024 and from time to time i have seen posts in here debating the merits of using annual leave when sick leave could have been used with many people saying that banking sick leave is a lousy investment with low return if added on your total time in service with others saying it is good to bank it for a health emergency if you can i have also read with laughter tears all of the wtf questions and answers surrounding telework and whether rto will happen or not when nobody really knows i am more frustrated at the posturing by people on the hill and the socalled doge wanting to mandate absolute rto especially as a means to reduce headcounts

what is frustrating about reading answers to these questions is the absolute certainty and associated arrogance that seems to come in those answers as a tailend boomer who spent 26 years in procurement with many of those years being a contracting officer let me say with my absolute certainty and associated arrogance is that the answer to this question and many questions when it comes to the federal government is really it depends on the situation or individual circumstances

my experience in 20132014 and beyond are perfect examples of this and how management can make things happen even though there are those who are certain they cannot be

i want to share my personal experience on how these things tied together saved my family financially and actually changed the trajectory of my career

from 20122014 i worked in sea02 contracting of naval sea systems command in washington dc i was geobaching it with my residence and family in georgia while i lived and worked in dc during the week except when i was in travel mode i was able to take advantage of a provision of the travel regulations that allowed me to start and end my official travel from either by duty station or my home of record doing this i could bookend my travel with weekends at home with my family so i could pay one roundtrip fare from dchome and get two weekends out of it

12 years ago today my daughter dropped me at the airport shuttle as i was travelling to san diego to conduct a followup ppmap inspection of a field activity little did i know that might be the last time i saw her alive

on friday january 11 2013 i was returning home via atl while waiting for my baggage i saw i had a message on my phone from a friend to say the message was a gut punch is to put it mildly my daughter had been hit by a motor vehicle while running suffered a severe traumatic brain injury and was rushed to a hospital with my friend not knowing which hospital

when i got to the hospital two hours later i found her in a coma with all kinds of tubes and wires coming out of her with machines beeping and a ventilator keeping her breathing steady if you have never experienced this it is more than overwhelming as there is nothing you can do is sit and wait and wait and pray and wait i looked at my leave balances a few days later to see what i had available it was not a pretty mix and was unlikely to last for the duration i was going to have to figure something out and try to negotiate with my boss

i took a week of leave that following week as i had to deal with insurance financial family logistics etc

as most of you especially in dod know teleworking was has been and continues to be a fourletter word ancient hierarchal management processes dictate a butts in seats rule as they only seemed to be able to manage you if they could see you in a seat not by your output and outcomes

surprisingly i was able to cut a deal with them i was allowed to plug in my laptop at the hospital vpn into our network and work when able if i had to stop work to meet with doctors or attend to other issues i put in the appropriate leave slip i chose to burn through my annual leave first and then sick leave and this continued for 34 weeks at the acute care facility and then for the next six months at the rehab facility in atlanta

if this had not been allowed i would have burned through all of my leave in a few months and forced into a lwop situation people had offered to donate leave but that is never a guarantee this would have meant financial doom for my family as my spouse was forced to quit their job because they were unable to work the irony was that she worked at the hospital where my daughter was in acute care

it is amazing how flexible things can be when onhigh management wants to be

now we switch to where teleworkingremote took over from the leave balance situation

all good things must come to an end and navsea wanted me back in dc my niece came to town to help my wife for a few months so that i could return to dc as required as her time to return home was nearing it was clear that my wife could not handle all of the caregiving work alone

at this point i had transferred to the buying floor from the head shop policy and as an organization we were reeling from the september shootingsdeaths in our offices our command and office had been split physically across many locations across the national capital region and we were just in the process of reconstituting the command in a new temporary headquarters location at buzzards point in dc the old coast guard hq that was slated for demolition

i went back to my bosses to see what we could do

my new division director said no to a return to telecommuting for a set period of time  he felt that as i was new to the team i needed to be in dc to interact facetoface with the program office i would be supporting  and there was also a practical reason  we were still a paper file driven office an electronic filing system was still a pipe dream ways off

serendipitously sea02 popped his head into my cube to see how things were going almost right after the division director said no  i told him what the decision was and he said to standby and he would talk to people to see what can be figured out

he came back to me a short while with the solution  they would reassign me back to my old job in the head shop where i would not have to be onsite change my duty location with locality pay reduced to rus as required and allow me to work remotely for a set period of time until my daughter was able to return to school and move into a dorm

it is amazing how flexible things can be when onhigh management wants to be

all was good during this time  i was able to work fulltime taking leave when needed to support my wife in caregiving responsibilities  yet lingering in the air was the notion i could not go back to dc and i started looking at two opportunities that would allow me to be closer to home or the ability to telework four days a week despite having to downgrade from a 13 to a 12  returning to the naval surface warfare center in panama city fl or apply for a job with gsa fas assisted acquisition services 

applying for jobs in usa jobs can be a crapshoot but before long i had offers from both entities 

 nswcpcd with a pay band equivalent for a gs 12 step 10 and no telework but closer to home six hour drive with a signing bonus or

 gsa in atlanta with a 12 step 10 and four days a week telework

i did not want to leave navsea as i had been mapping pout the rest of my career to be with them but family does and always wins i chose the gsa offer and as i had to be in the office one day a week i qualified for atlanta locality pay vs rest of us the pay area border literally ended at the county line 13 miles from my house that year but a year or two later we were melded into the atl locality area  like people in dc we had a transit subsidy allowing me to take a commuter bus in but still had to pay for my own gas for the 45 minute each way drive to the bus stop  the commute would take 23 hours each way depending on traffic and weather

as i was transitioning to this new opportunity i had to return to dc to turn in my equipment and go through the lengthy manual checkout process  i took the opportunity to request an exit interview with sea02 thank him for his extreme flexibility in my situation and give him some feedback on navseas telework processes

i told him point blank 

you have an eeo sue me sign planted squarely on your backside just waiting to be kicked  you have no written telework policy and managers say fulltime telework is not available to employees with rare exceptions  yet you have four people teleworking fulltime including one from singapore because her husband pcsd there and another one 15 miles away because they just had a baby  all women  no men  it wont be me but believe me you someone will tee this up unless you get your act together on this and come up with a written policy

note  ironically i was told the division director who had said no to me teleworking quit in protest when he was being pressuredforced to get people back in the office during covid  i do not know that this is true but just had to shake my head when i heard about it

fast forward to 20192020 and covid  there was only one agency truly ready to go fulltime remote immediately  gsa  because that is how we had operated for years  i cannot begin to tell you the frustrations dealing with our federal customers who could not connect to their systems from home to conduct business   you know the edict that people should not use personal email accounts to conduct business  yeah right

i cannot begin to express my anger with one federal customer who demanded that the four ftes on a newly awarded contract be onsite something the contractor faced inordinate obstacles in accomplishing because of covid  the contract was failing miserably and they were far from the only ones having this problem and the customer was livid blaming the contractor  it got to the point i that i had to schedule a ctj conference call with the onestar commander and ask him how it was that their equivalent national guard component had a contract for identical services and the contractor was allowed to work fully remote before covid  were they my customer actually engaged in an illegal personal services contract relationship

they acquiesced and agreed to allow the contractor to work remotely on a test basis  i said no for the remainder of the base period and all of the option periods

not only did the contractor fill all of the positions quickly with people from across the country performance was at levels the federal customer had not seen in years

it is amazing how productive people can be offsite

as the covid emergency was coming to an end my coworkers and i were given a choice

1  return to precovid state and the four day a week telework with one day in office to retain atl locality or

2  convert to 100 remote with the understanding that pay would be set based on locality pay for our home addresses as that would be our duty station 

for me it was a nobrainer  fulltime remote  for others that lived in rus areas they were willing to take the pay cut not have to deal with atlanta traffic and long drives 34 hours each way to be in the office one day a week

again it is amazing how flexible things can be when onhigh management wants to be

finally thoughts on telework and rto as i no longer have a dog in this fight

if members of congress actually had a clue on how things really work especially paywise they would not be introducing soundbite baseinciting stupid bills like the one that says that if someone teleworks their pay will be cut from locality pay as they are not in the actual office  i will not use the words i want to say about this because to quite a legendary jesuit priests dcbased homily once they would not exactly be pulpit language

if only i could have 15 minutes with these members over a beer or sweet tea

i am a priormilitary and a boomer and if my boss says you need to be in the office the answer is threebags full when do i have to be back in the office as i am making clear that it sucks but those are the marching orders  and yes i would be looking for other jobs that would fit my needs and goals but i would not quit unless i had one

at the same time i loved being able to telework so much and felt more productive doing so than ever in an office that did not have highperforming teams  it also enabled me to be there for my daughter and family when they needed me most

dont get me wrong  there are some things in my mind that have to or should be done face to face  like longterm instructor led training in your career fields  offsite inperson technical evaluation panels for competitive contract awards are much more efficient and less prone to having members pulled out of their offices for other things when doing them remotely

and yes i missed going four years of not seeing my coworkers in person and catching up in the flesh  but one presupposition is that you are all in the office on the same day another is that you actually have office space to return to 

some years ago they shut down our leased offices in midtown atlanta and made us move to the martin luther king building in the high crime area of five points all the way downtown in atlanta if you saw the opening episode of the walking dead  you have seen the building

being the shy retiring personality i am i loudly balked at this move over the safety issues and knowing how such a move ibm imposed on my lotus office in the 00s totally destroyed the communal collaborative processes and workspaces we had in turn killing productivity and revenue production and that despite the gsa  management pr that we were just doing what they are doing in the private sector they somehow missed the memo that the private sector had for years been retreating from this model

in this new space we would have no assigned offices just hotdesks that we could not permanently reserve  as a result our staff ended up spread out over two sprawling floors of space and nobody had an office we could meet in  we had to hope we could reserve a conference room for an adhoc meeting  the noise levels were unbearable and made it difficult to work

in august 2023 i had to convene a weeklong technical evaluation panel at the mlk building bosses mandate that it had to be inperson  no one had told us that half of our space had been taken away and given to the epa and that our codes would no longer work  no one told me that the guest wifi was not functional and that my dod customers could not get online  no one told me that the federal cafeterias were closed and that we would have to navigate throngs of aggressive homeless people and panhandlers to get anyplace to get food for lunch  return to office  i do not think so

a return to office guide i made a few years ago before i joined the government when i was a manager a few years ago we initiated a massive rto push for our employees to assist with the transition i created this guide for my team and other managers over the past two weeks i took some time to update it for the federal workforce in preparation for our eventual push back to the office

this guide should be taken with a grain of salt and used as more of a preparation checklist or conversation starter with your management id also like to remind you of the two major reasons behind this rto

1 to enable layoffs without having to pay severance
2 to support local dc businesses

 before rto is implemented

1 plan your commute  
the first thing to consider is how youll get to the office my guide focuses heavily on dc since thats where im based

 parking does your office have enough parking for everyone who drives in whats the process for requesting a parking pass if parking passes are limited does the office cover or provide discounts for garages
    check nearby garages for monthly rates which could save you hundreds of dollars a year many garages also offer early bird specials for arrivals before 6 am
 tolls and traffic use google maps to identify toll roads and estimate your commute time add an extra 1015 to your estimate for a more realistic outlook if your commute involves crossing the 495 bridge prepare for heavy traffic will your tolls be set or will they change based on traffics should you carpool 
 public transit if youre using public transit ensure you enroll in the transit subsidy program youre eligible for up to 315 a month
    for metro riders parking costs 499 per day check if your station has parking and consider nearby garages for better rates

2 understand expectations

 core hours most offices require employees to be available during those hours ask what those hours are can you work from home outside of those hours are you allowed to leave before the core hours end
 breaks understand the policy for breaks some managers or agencies dont allow you to stack breaks eg combining a 30minute lunch with two 15minute breaks for a 60minute lunch
 overtime policy determine if youre exempt or nonexempt and familiarize yourself with your offices overtime policy remember you must work 40 hours but if you have to work 1 more hour you need to get ot remember need it in writing from your manager that they approve it 
 rto timeline once rto is announced find out how much time you have to comply chances are it will not be a day 

 rto is now implemented  now what

 transition period full implementation may take weeks or months as offices prepare spaces verify badge functionality configure desktops and arrange seating wait for official agency guidance avoid relying on tweets or unofficial sources your supervisor will inform you when you need to come in
 attendance tracking find out how rto compliance will be tracked will it require badge swipes periodic teams checkins or another method knowing this can help reduce stress and plan your day
 telework agreements if telework agreements are voided and youre expected to work during opm closures ensure management provides written expectations if not enjoy your snow days

 youre back in the office  now what

 bring your own lunch avoid frequent purchases from dcarea businesses as one purpose of rto is to support local businesses
 maintain positivity keep a positive attitude this situation is temporary and likely wont be as bad as anticipated help foster a positive office environmentit starts with you
 union support stay in touch with your union and ensure agreements are being honored report any issues to your union representative

at the end of the day we have no idea what is going to happen in 2448 hours or next four years the only thing we can control is our attitude strive to work on our agency mission and serve the american people

my rto grievance arguments fns employee under nteu cba wondered if others would like to see an example of a untested grievance so i figured id share the gist of what ive got written up in mine im not suggesting anyone take my arguments wholesale because these are my interpretations of our cba and federal laws you should independently review anything ive said and determine if you agree or not and to what extent also some of these are complete hail marys truly a long shot at best 

that being said hopefully these offer a good jumping off point for anyone else that wants to file a grievance

 cba is binding  i reference the cba and opms website  which state that the cba generally binds the union and the agency to its conditions this is just to establish the authority of the cba and that the agency has a responsibility to follow it
 violation 1 the agency failed to comply with the cba by making a unilateral change to a personnel policy practice or condition of employment
    cba says in section 53 the employer agrees not to unilaterally establish or change any personnel policy practice or condition of employment which terminates or conflicts with specific terms or conditions of this agreement
    telework is a personnel policy practice or condition of employment because 5 usc 7103a14 defines condition of employment as  14 conditions of employment means personnel policies practices and matters whether established by rule regulation or otherwise affecting working conditions 
    as written the cba references to usda dr 4080811002 and section 4a of that states that usda fully supports and promotes telework while yes the acting secretary did revoke that rule thats just more evidence that they unilaterally changed a policy otherwise section 20 of the cba is the policy surrounding telework
    therefore by revoking all telework except for rare circumstances usda unilaterally changing its policy around telework which it previously supportedpromoted is in direct violation of the cba
 violation 2 a lack of a replacement departmental regulation regarding telework violates the telework enhancement act
    not actually finished with this one yet because we havent received the official back to the office this day email
    but 5 usc 6502 requires departments to have a telework policy that was dr 4080811002 and without that usda is in violation of the law
       i dont know if this will matter but ill include it in the grievance either way if there isnt one by the time i file it
 violation 3 reducing telework and remote work violates the purpose of the telework enhancement act and public law 106346 title iii section 359
    basically its the telework enhancement act that names has meaning its the intention of the bill
    i also refer to 5 usc 6506 which says agencies shall submit reports that include 
       d the agency goal for increasing participation to the extent practicable or necessary for the next reporting period as indicated by the percent of eligible employees teleworking in each frequency category described under subparagraph aiii  
       e an explanation of whether or not the agency met the goals for the last reporting period and if not what actions are being taken to identify and eliminate barriers to maximizing telework opportunities for the next reporting period 
    both of those sections talk about increasing telework and remote work in some capacity so thats further evidence that the intention is not to limit telework
    also pl 106346 title iii section 359 is still an active law which states each executive agency shall establish a policy under which eligible employees of the agency may participate in telecommuting to the maximum extent possible without diminished employee performance while it does say may it also says to the maximum extent possible which clearly indicates departments should expand telework not limit it
 violation 4 requiring a return to the main office unfairly discriminates against based on conduct that does not negatively impact my performance
    this ones definitely a long shot
    basically 5 usc 2302b10 and the section 3703j of the cba prevent discrimination based on conduct unrelated to an employees ability to perform their jobs
       i argue elsewhere that my job has an easy numerical statistic to prove im able to do my job so that will kind of depend on your own situation
    i argue that the conduct in question is choosing to live away from the office and use the home as the office so because the trump administration folks have argued that people arent able to do their jobs while remote working that this is discrimination based on anecdotal evidence from the larger group
 other considerations
    not violations of law but i also include a section of other facts to consider such as
       like i said easily tracked data that i complete my job more than satisfactorily
       requiring me to work at my home office would change my locality pay and would actually cost taxpayers 10k more per year
       we were not giving guidance of what a qualifying medical condition would be so that we could still try to work from home



  remedies
    the remedies i request are
       reinstatement of telework
       temporary reinstatement during the grievance process
       any other appropriate remedy

what did we learn  
we found that jobrelated outcomes were the same for remote workers and teleworkers with no statistically significant differences in employee outcomes performance ratings among remote workers and teleworkers were almost identical remote workers were rated 001 point less than teleworkers on a 5 point scale remote workers took the same number of sick days days of family leave and worked the same number of hours as teleworkers remote workers transferred to other parts of the federal government at the same rate as teleworkers and were 05 percentage points more likely to  transfer within gsa none of the differences were statistically significant

we find a 12 percentage point decrease in the proportion of remote workers exiting the federal workforce compared with teleworkers this estimate falls short of the adjusted threshold for statistical significance

bus code 7777 explained or how to form a bargaining unit if the bus code on your sf50 says 7777 it means that the duties and scope of your position allow you to be eligible to be part of a bargaining unit but that your place of employment does not have one most federal agencies are not unionized across the board bargaining units form at the unit program center whatever level if you want to be part of a union then you and your colleagues will need to do the hard work of organizing and forming a bargaining unit its not a lost cause but it will take time here are the basic steps that will get you towards that goal

1 find a few colleagues and form a small organizing team that will help with outreach to the rest of your unit although organizing is protected by law its recommended that you do not put term or probationary employees on your organizing team you should aim to define your unit as a large enough group of people to make bargaining worthwhile 50100 is small  ideally you would have many hundreds

2 create your own org chart or workplace map to help you figure out who else is eligible to be part of the unit should be anyone other than supervisors and management officials use your organizing team to divide up the list and start talking to those who are eligible if you are in person discussing unionizing is considered water cooler conversation and is allowed by law if you are still on remote or telework i would strongly suggest using coded language on government systems and taking conversations to personal devices as soon as possible

3 in parallel with 2 youll need to identify what union you want to form under eg nteu afge and get a rep who will support you through the process they all have cold call forms on their websites but they are being slammed right now by panicking federal employees if you know of another bargaining unit in your agency try to reach out and see if theyll share the name of their union rep so that you can contact someone directly

4 you will need to collect showing of interest cards from eligible employees who want to form a bargaining unit these showing of interest cards are specific to the union organization with which you are working  they say that you want to form a bargaining unit and that x organization is the sole organization that can represent you by law you only need to collect cards from 30 of your eligible employees but most groups aim for 50 or more to help them figure out if theyll win the election and to demonstrate strength to the agency

5 your union rep will take the cards youve collected and file an official petition with the federal labor relations authority flra this will trigger a notice to your agency and they will be required to post official notices physically and electronically telling employees that a petition has been filed at this point you might receive interest and questions from the people you havent already talked to

6 the agency will be asked to provide the flra with a list of who they consider to be eligible to be part of the bargaining unit importantly even if someone was coded as 7777 the agency can contest their eligibility at this time the flra tries to settle these disputes through informal negotiations but if both parties reach an impasse then it can go to an official hearing the flra website has tons of resources on case law and precedent but it does take time and effort to find the answers you need

7 if the agency and the union agree on the list of eligible employees congrats you can now hold a vote to form your bargaining unit then you begin the hard work of drafting and negotiating your collective bargaining agreement

  
this whole process plus negotiating the cba can easily take over a year and in some cases multiple years like i said its hard work but it can be done

there is not yet any evidence the administration can or will uphold its end of the bargain that congress will go along with this unilateral massive restructuring or that appropriated funds can be used this way among other issues that have been raised we are encouraging afge members not to resign or respond to this email until you have received further information and clarification

frequently asked questions faqs on opms deferred resignation program email

what is the deferred resignation program
the deferred resignation program program was introduced by an email sent to federal employees on january 28 2025 preceded by threats to modify and downsize the federal workforce the program purports to allow federal employees to submit a resignation letter that will become effective on september 30 2025 in exchange the program claims that employees will be exempt from return to office requirements and will maintain their current compensation and benefits until the effective date of their resignation

employees should not take the program at face value the program documentation including the introductory email an associated guidance memorandum issued by the office of personnel management opm on january 28 2025 and opmissued faqs are riddled with inconsistencies and uncertainties it is also unclear whether opm has the legal authority to support the program or its alleged benefits and the eligibility criteria are vague

is the program a buyout
no the program is not buyout nor is it a voluntary separation incentive payment visp program instead it purports to offer employees the ability to submit a deferred resignation and claims employees that do so will continue to receive pay while still possibly working until september 30 2025

notably however the program contains no guarantee that an employees resignation will be accepted nor does the program guarantee that an employees whose resignation is accepted will receive the benefits that the program purports to offer

if an employee chooses to accept the program are they required to work during the deferred resignation period
they may be opms statements are conflicting on this point according to the opm email and letter employees will not be required to work in person but may be assigned remote work duties the opm faq page also suggests that employees will not be required to work except in rare cases without defining what constitutes rare cases at the same time the faqs describe the deferred resignation period as a nice vacation and the program states that employees may be placed on paid administrative leave

can an employee take another job during the deferred resignation period
the faq states that the resignation letter does not explicitly prohibit outside employment however other existing policies such as agencyspecific regulations requiring prior authorization for outside work are likely to apply

are all federal employees eligible for the program
no employees in positions related to immigration enforcement and national security as well as those in any positions specifically excluded by their employing agency are not eligible usps employees and military personnel are also excluded there is no guidance on how employees can confirm their eligibility or if their agency has specific exclusions

will employees who optin be protected from termination before their resignation date
nothing in the program documentation purports to prohibit the termination or separation of an employee who accepts deferred resignation while the opm email suggests that employees will maintain their compensation and benefits until the effective date of their resignation date it does not explicitly state that employees are shielded from layoffs or other adverse actions before september 30 2025 there is no guarantee that employees opting in to the program will not be targeted for such actions

the program also does not indicate what may occur in the event of a lapse in congressional appropriations at present many agencies of the federal government are only funded through march 14 2025

what happens if an agency requires an employee to continue working despite opms faq stating that continued work should be rare
while opms faq states that work will only be required in rare cases the programs details vary across the different opm documents if an agency insists on continued work employees may not have a clear administrative remedy as the enforceability of the promises and statements in opms faq is uncertain

what legal recourse do employees have if the government does not honor the terms of deferred resignation
it is unclear what recourse if any employees might have if the government fails to honor the terms of their deferred resignation there is no certainty that the statements made in the opm program documents will be legally enforceable even if the email and faq page are interpreted as an implied contract or offer there is no guarantee that such a claim would be enforceable for example while each case will be factspecific resignation is generally considered to be a voluntary action it is therefore unclear whether violations of the policy would be appealable to the merit systems protection board through the grievance process or any other forum

how can employees ensure the administration will follow through on the program
given the inconsistencies between programs various documents issued by opm as well as the ambiguous and conflicting language regarding work obligations and exclusions there is no guarantee that the claims in the program will be honored by the government the program may also face legal challenges that could alter the terms of all or portions of the program employees who optin to the program will be at the mercy of the administrators of the program whose claims contain inconsistencies and lack stated legal underpinning

is there an assurance that the promised continued salary will be funded
no nothing in the opm documentation contains such an assurance moreover because current appropriations for most civilian agencies are set to expire march 14 2025 it is not guaranteed that agencies affected by the current appropriations bill will continue to have adequate funding for the promised salary beyond the bills expiration

what actions can locals and councils take to protect bargaining unit employees from the program
locals and councils may

consider filing requests for information under 5 usc  7114b4
consider filing a demand to bargain over the program
consider grievances alleging the program violates terms of their collective bargaining agreement or regulations eg regulations concerning administrative leave
locals and councils may also have a basis for a grievance or unfair labor practice charge alleging among other things a bypass of the union with respect to communications about the program directly to employees

aflcio fed employee union response to letter just wanted to share this in case it hasnt been yet



our union became aware yesterday that afge members were sent an email asking you to resign from federal service with a vague promise of reward for resigning by february 6


there is not yet any evidence the administration can or will uphold its end of the bargain that congress will go along with this unilateral massive restructuring or that appropriated funds can be used this way among other issues that have been raised we are encouraging afge members not to resign or respond to this email until you have received further information and clarification


in the meantime we have developed some frequently asked questions to provide you with the best guidance we can given the current uncertainty


frequently asked questions faqs on opms deferred resignation program email


what is the deferred resignation program
the deferred resignation program program was introduced by an email sent to federal employees on january 28 2025 preceded by threats to modify and downsize the federal workforce the program purports to allow federal employees to submit a resignation letter that will become effective on september 30 2025 in exchange the program claims that employees will be exempt from return to office requirements and will maintain their current compensation and benefits until the effective date of their resignation


employees should not take the program at face value the program documentation including the introductory email an associated guidance memorandum issued by the office of personnel management opm on january 28 2025 and opmissued faqs are riddled with inconsistencies and uncertainties it is also unclear whether opm has the legal authority to support the program or its alleged benefits and the eligibility criteria are vague


is the program a buyout
no the program is not buyout nor is it a voluntary separation incentive payment visp program instead it purports to offer employees the ability to submit a deferred resignation and claims employees that do so will continue to receive pay while still possibly working until september 30 2025


notably however the program contains no guarantee that an employees resignation will be accepted nor does the program guarantee that an employees whose resignation is accepted will receive the benefits that the program purports to offer


if an employee chooses to accept the program are they required to work during the deferred resignation period
they may be opms statements are conflicting on this point according to the opm email and letter employees will not be required to work in person but may be assigned remote work duties the opm faq page also suggests that employees will not be required to work except in rare cases without defining what constitutes rare cases at the same time the faqs describe the deferred resignation period as a nice vacation and the program states that employees may be placed on paid administrative leave


can an employee take another job during the deferred resignation period
the faq states that the resignation letter does not explicitly prohibit outside employment however other existing policies such as agencyspecific regulations requiring prior authorization for outside work are likely to apply


are all federal employees eligible for the program
no employees in positions related to immigration enforcement and national security as well as those in any positions specifically excluded by their employing agency are not eligible usps employees and military personnel are also excluded there is no guidance on how employees can confirm their eligibility or if their agency has specific exclusions


will employees who optin be protected from termination before their resignation date
nothing in the program documentation purports to prohibit the termination or separation of an employee who accepts deferred resignation while the opm email suggests that employees will maintain their compensation and benefits until the effective date of their resignation date it does not explicitly state that employees are shielded from layoffs or other adverse actions before september 30 2025 there is no guarantee that employees opting in to the program will not be targeted for such actions


the program also does not indicate what may occur in the event of a lapse in congressional appropriations at present many agencies of the federal government are only funded through march 14 2025


what happens if an agency requires an employee to continue working despite opms faq stating that continued work should be rare
while opms faq states that work will only be required in rare cases the programs details vary across the different opm documents if an agency insists on continued work employees may not have a clear administrative remedy as the enforceability of the promises and statements in opms faq is uncertain


what legal recourse do employees have if the government does not honor the terms of deferred resignation
it is unclear what recourse if any employees might have if the government fails to honor the terms of their deferred resignation there is no certainty that the statements made in the opm program documents will be legally enforceable even if the email and faq page are interpreted as an implied contract or offer there is no guarantee that such a claim would be enforceable for example while each case will be factspecific resignation is generally considered to be a voluntary action it is therefore unclear whether violations of the policy would be appealable to the merit systems protection board through the grievance process or any other forum


how can employees ensure the administration will follow through on the program
given the inconsistencies between programs various documents issued by opm as well as the ambiguous and conflicting language regarding work obligations and exclusions there is no guarantee that the claims in the program will be honored by the government the program may also face legal challenges that could alter the terms of all or portions of the program employees who optin to the program will be at the mercy of the administrators of the program whose claims contain inconsistencies and lack stated legal underpinning


is there an assurance that the promised continued salary will be funded
no nothing in the opm documentation contains such an assurance moreover because current appropriations for most civilian agencies are set to expire march 14 2025 it is not guaranteed that agencies affected by the current appropriations bill will continue to have adequate funding for the promised salary beyond the bills expiration

legal and policy justifications for an ergonomic workspace
rehabilitation act of 1973 section 501  504
as a federal employee you are protected under the rehabilitation act of 1973 which requires federal agencies to provide reasonable accommodations to employees with disabilities or medical conditions
if your issues are documented you can formally request reasonable accommodations for a standing desk ergonomic chair and ergonomic workstation setup
americans with disabilities act ada 42 usc  12101 et seq
while the ada primarily applies to private sector employers and statelocal governments federal agencies adhere to similar requirements under the rehabilitation act
if your condition substantially limits major life activities such as sitting or working comfortably an ergonomic setup can be considered a reasonable accommodation
executive order 13164 requiring federal agencies to establish procedures for reasonable accommodation
this order mandates that federal agencies develop policies and processes to reasonably accommodate employees with medical needs this includes ergonomic office furniture

this osha document was not adopted but contains good language for reuse but do not cite this osha guidance directly   draftoccupational safety and health administration osha ergonomics guidance
osha 29 cfr 1910900draft outlines workplace ergonomics and encourages agencies to provide employees with adjustable desks ergonomic chairs and proper workstation setups to prevent workrelated musculoskeletal disorders
federal agencies typically have occupational safety and health osh offices that handle ergonomic evaluations and accommodations
agencyspecific workplace accommodation programs
many federal agencies have internal disability accommodation programs daps or reasonable accommodation coordinators who process ergonomic furniture requests
agencies often cover costs for standing desks ergonomic chairs keyboardmouse accommodations and other workstation adjustments under their workplace safety and health budgets
steps to request an ergonomic setup
medical documentation if required
you may need a note from your healthcare provider stating that a standing desk and ergonomic chair are necessary to prevent aggravation of your backspine condition
your doctor should describe the specific limitations and recommend appropriate accommodations
formal request for reasonable accommodation
submit a written request to your supervisor hr or agencys reasonable accommodation coordinator
cite the rehabilitation act osha ergonomics guidelines and agency policies as justification
specify the exact accommodations you need eg electric sitstand desk ergonomic chair with lumbar support adjustable monitor setup
engage in the interactive process
your agency is required to engage in discussions with you about your request
if your agency denies the request they must provide a valid reason and you have the right to appeal
leverage agency ergonomic programs
many agencies already have ergonomic assessment programs in place
ask if your agency provides funding for ergonomic evaluations and equipment

appeal if denied

if your request is denied you can appeal through
the equal employment opportunity eeo office within your agency
filing a grievance under your union if applicable
seeking help from the office of special counsel osc or merit systems protection board mspb

additional considerations
if your agency has flexible work arrangements you might also inquire about hybrid work options as an alternative accommodation

if you are a veteran with a serviceconnected disability you may have additional rights through the department of veterans affairs for workplace accommodations

congressional interest in expanding the use of telework in the executive branch began in earnest with the passage of the transportation and related agencies appropriations act of 2001 public law 106346 external link pdf file required each executive agency to establish a policy under which eligible employees of the agency would be permitted to participate in telework to the maximum extent possible without diminished employee performance  the act required opm to ensure that these telework requirements were applied to 25 percent of the federal workforce within six months of enactment and to an additional 25 percent of employees every year thereafter

what to the federal worker is presidents day fellow americans colleagues and civil servants

i stand before you on this presidents day a day set aside to honor the legacies of those who have occupied the highest office in our land it is a day draped in history wrapped in patriotic ceremony and imbued with reverence for the ideals of leadership the nation commemorates its presidentspast and presentwith speeches with tributes and with a moments pause to reflect on the offices grandeur but what is this day to the federal worker

to the federal worker presidents day is not merely a day of remembranceit is a mirror reflecting the vast chasm between leadership and those who toil beneath its weight it is a day of paradoxes where the noble rhetoric of governance is overshadowed by the grim realities of bureaucracy inequity and disregard

the presidents name is invoked in sweeping declarations of democracy and progress but what of the federal worker who carries out the daytoday labor of the republic what of those who keep its systems runningthose who process its policies protect its people and uphold its laws we are the unseen machinery of this nation expected to function without fail even as we are neglected silenced and in times of crisis discarded

what to the federal worker is presidents day when the very institutions we serve fail to recognize our worth when administrations come and go often using us as pawns in political games shutting down the government freezing our pay questioning our integrity and stripping us of dignity in the name of efficiency we are expected to serve without question without protest and without fair compensation for the sacrifices we endure

what to the federal worker is presidents day when promises of respect and recognition ring hollow when the public scoffs at the notion of government service painting us as burdens rather than as the backbone of a functioning society when we are maligned even as we labor through crises from natural disasters to public health emergencies ensuring that the very fabric of this nation does not unravel

the past year alone has shown the fragile nature of our positionsthreats to our security our benefits our ability to telework and perform our duties effectively some among us have endured workplace hostility discrimination and systemic neglect we have been told that our work matters while simultaneously being denied the conditions necessary to perform it with dignity and fairness

presidents day to many is a day of pride and honor to us it is a day of reckoninga moment to reflect on the sacrifices made by those who serve without recognition without the prestige of high office without the protection of power it is a day to ask who will lead not only with words but with actions who will recognize that the foundation of their power rests upon the unyielding labor of public servants

so let us not simply observe this day as a tribute to those who have governed let us reclaim it as a demand for justice a reminder that leadership is not measured by title alone but by its treatment of those who make governance possible let presidents day be not only a celebration of the past but a call to action for the futurewhere the dignity of public service is not a footnote in history but its guiding principle

to my fellow federal workers let us stand together not just in duty but in dignity let our voices be heard our work be valued and our service be honorednot with empty praise but with real and lasting change

for if this nation is to celebrate its leaders let it first recognize those who keep it standing

heres what every federal government worker should know as more executive orders are rolled out and what i predict may happen next

rto mandates will include most federal employees but there are exemptions

the united states office of personal management opm issued guidance that targets both remote and teleworkers in the returntooffice mandates

remote workers are people who live outside of the commuting area and teleworkers are folks who are based in the commuting area but still work from home

those exempted from the returntooffice mandates are people with reasonable accommodations or people with a qualifying disability those with a qualifying disability are presumably disabled people who had been working from home but never needed to formalize it into reasonable accommodation until now

theres also an exemption for those with a compelling reason we dont know exactly what that covers yet but agencies will certainly have some discretion over what that means the most recent guidance referenced an exemption for military spouses

federal deia workers might be assigned to new roles with some similar tasks

employees working in deia groups were placed on paid administrative leave also reduction in force notices which are essentially 60day layoff notices were issued to some folks

the reduction in force process is governed by very complex regulations so well have to see how much the  administration cares to abide by those regulations

so far they havent been terribly concerned with complying whats murky is that some of the deia employees are reasonable accommodation coordinators a function that still needs to be performed i predict some folks will be reassigned to different roles but still tasked with performing that function

the hiring freeze is messier than it should be and might last for a while

the opm guidance says that any federal government job offer signed after january 20 at noon is invalid and those positions will remain vacant

ive heard from folks who say they thought they secured a federal agency job months ago but still got their offers rescinded this may be because a lot of times the government issues tentative job offers months before making firm offers

i always advise people not to give notice to their current employer until they have signed the firm final offer i predict the hiring freeze may continue for a while

its best to comply now and complain later

unless ordered to do something unsafe my golden rule for federal employees is comply now complain later 

even if you think youre being ordered to do something that violates agency policy or goes against your belief system there may be consequences for failing to comply

for example if you refuse a reassignment the government may just fire you if youre fired its incredibly difficult to get rehired or file a complaint youll be fighting an uphill battle

being employed by the government is what gives you leverage to challenge an order you dont agree with

id recommend that the same employee take the reassignment and then file a grievance equal opportunity complaint or merit systems protection board appeal depending on the situation there are several avenues to complain through and because those resources were set up by federal law theyre not going anywhere

the meetings themselves varied in tone and scope but their regularity was a constant some were brief checkins lasting no more than fifteen minutes where id offer a quick update on my progress and hear from others about theirs others stretched into hourlong discussions diving into the weeds of specific challenges or brainstorming solutions to unexpected hurdles regardless of their length or intensity i approached each one with the same mindset this was my opportunity to connect to calibrate and to push my work ahead id arrive prepared often with notes scribbled from the previous session or a mental checklist of what i needed to share about my normal projectsthose tasks that while not always headlinegrabbing formed the backbone of my responsibilities


why did i go to these meetings so faithfully the answer lies in their purpose they werent just gatherings for the sake of gathering they were engines of progress by attending i ensured i wasnt working in a vacuum my normal projectsthings like drafting reports refining processes or managing incremental updates to larger initiativesdidnt exist in isolation they were part of a broader ecosystem one that relied on communication and coordination the meetings gave me a window into that ecosystem letting me see where my efforts fit and how they overlapped with or depended on the work of others id sit there listening as a colleague described a delay in their timeline and realize i needed to adjust my own schedule accordingly or id hear about a new priority from a supervisor and understand instantly how it would reshape the direction of my tasks


this routine of attendance began to feel almost ritualistic but in the best possible way it was like clockwork monday mornings might mean a team huddle to set the weeks tone wednesday afternoons could bring a deeper dive with a smaller subgroup and fridays often wrapped up with a recap to tie loose ends before the weekend i didnt just go because i had to i went because i wanted to there was a satisfaction in the predictability a comfort in knowing that no matter how chaotic my individual workload became these meetings would provide a touchstonea moment to pause assess and realign and through it all my normal projects kept advancing not in leaps and bounds but in the steady reliable increments that come from consistent effort

bill overview

 title to prohibit certain telework employees from receiving certain annual adjustments to pay schedules and for other purposes
 bill number hr236
 introduced date january 7 2025
 sponsor representative dan newhouse rwa
 cosponsors representatives zachary nunn ria dan meuser rpa randy weber rtx lauren boebert rco william timmons rsc jake ellzey rtx ashley hinson ria mike collins rga nicole malliotakis rny earl carter rga brad finstad rmn and charles fleischmann rtn
 committee referral referred to the house committee on oversight and government reform

purpose

the bill aims to adjust the pay structure for federal employees who telework specifically it proposes that employees who telework at least one day per week should

 annual adjustments be excluded from receiving annual pay adjustments under section 5303 of title 5 united states code
 locality pay receive basic pay corresponding to the rest of us locality pay area regardless of their official duty stations location

exemptions

the bill does not apply to certain categories of employees including

 those receiving reasonable accommodations due to disabilities
 members of the foreign service
 federal law enforcement officers
 activeduty members of the armed forces

rationale

proponents of the bill argue that federal employees who telework from lowercost areas should not receive locality pay based on highercost office locations they cite concerns about efficient use of taxpayer funds and the underutilization of federal office spaces

current status

the bill is currently under consideration by the house committee on oversight and government reform no further actions have been recorded as of this date

according to the us office of personnel management opm remote work is defined as

remote work is a work arrangement in which an employee performs their duties from a location other than their official duty station and the employee is not expected to report to their official duty station on a regular and recurring basis

telework is a work arrangement in which an employee performs their duties from an approved alternative worksite such as their home on a regular and recurring basis but the employee is still expected to report to their official duty station on a periodic basis

1 the use of may in the tea

the telework enhancement act of 2010 tea requires agency heads to establish a policy under which eligible employees of the agency may be authorized to telework 5 usc  6502a1 the word may refers to granting agencies discretion to determine which employees are eligible for telework based on jobspecific responsibilities operational needs and other practical considerations however the statutes use of may does not mean agencies can avoid adopting a telework policy altogether instead it allows agencies flexibility to tailor telework policies while still requiring them to comply with the broader mandate to maximize telework

 2 may vs shall in context

in legal language shall typically creates a binding obligation if congress had written that agencies shall authorize all employees to telework this would create a mandatory telework requirement for all eligible employees in contrast may allows for discretion but it does not absolve the agency from compliance with the statutes overarching purpose in this case the tea requires agencies to establish policies to maximize telework while preserving operational efficiency and performance agencies may authorize telework for specific employees based on their eligibility but they cannot refuse to establish a policy altogether

 3 congresss intent in the tea

the legislative history of the tea underscores that its purpose was to promote telework to the maximum extent possible congress aimed to institutionalize telework in federal agencies not to make it optional

 section 6502a2 states that the head of each agency must ensure that the telework policy authorizes employees to telework to the maximum extent possible without diminishing agency operations and performance

the use of may reflects a recognition of the practical reality that not all employees or roles are suited for telework however this discretion is subordinate to the statutes broader requirement to maximize telework opportunities where feasible

 4 may does not negate accountability

even though may grants discretion agencies are still required to

 establish and maintain a telework policy  6502a1  
 evaluate employee eligibility for telework based on clear criteria  6502a1a  
 ensure that telework is considered as broadly as possible consistent with operational needs  6502a2 and  
 use telework as a tool for continuity of operations  6503a5

in short may governs how agencies apply telework policies but does not give them the option to ignore the tea entirely

 5 judicial interpretations of may

courts interpreting statutory language often balance the permissive language of may against the overall purpose of the statute in cases involving workplace rights or federal agency mandates courts have consistently held that discretion under may must still be exercised in good faith and in alignment with the statutes objectives 

for example

 if an agency failed to establish or maintain a telework policy this would likely be considered noncompliance with the tea  
 similarly if an agencys telework policy completely excluded telework without justification it might conflict with the statutes requirement to maximize telework opportunities

 6 conclusion

the inclusion of may in the telework enhancement act of 2010 reflects congresss intent to grant agencies flexibility in applying telework policies based on operational needs and employee roles however it does not negate the statutory requirement for agencies to establish telework policies evaluate employee eligibility and implement telework to the greatest extent feasible 

agencies are not required to authorize telework for all employees but they are required to comply with the tea by creating and maintaining policies that enable telework wherever possible attempts to completely eliminate telework as suggested by the opm memorandum risk conflicting with the teas core mandates even under a permissive may framework

from the eeocs website a disability is defined as a person who

has a physical or mental condition that substantially limits a major life activity such as walking talking seeing hearing or learning or operation of a major bodily function such as brain musculoskeletal respiratory circulatory or endocrine function

a medical condition does not need to be longterm permanent or severe to be substantially limiting  also if symptoms come and go what matters is how limiting the symptoms are when they are active

it is important for your doctor to 1 identify your disability 2 state the anticipated duration of your disability 3 recommend telework  and 4 note how telework will ameliorate the symptoms of your disability which will then allow you to fully perform the essential functions of your position

the agency does not have to provide you with the ra recommended by your doctor but they must engage with you in the interactive process ip after youve requested the ra for instance during the ip your agency may offer 5 days of telework per pay period rather than the full tw schedule your dr recommended the agency may also deny your request if they can show it would cause an undue hardship for them to provide the ra  

whats key for you to focus on is explaining to your agency how your disability will limit your work effectiveness and how telework will lessen the symptoms of your disability and enable you to fully perform your job duties

 plan requirements

agency implementation plans should include

1 steps to revise telework agreements for eligible employees

5 identification of potential risks barriers or resource constraints

6 process for determining exceptions based on disability medical conditions or other compelling reasons

7 criteria for granting exemptions from returntooffice requirements



 key principles

1 prioritize the return of headquarters and eligible employees who can return expeditiously

2 maximize use of existing federal space before adding new space

3 group employees based on duties and job functions to promote collaboration and effective management



 eligible employees

the memo defines eligible employees as all agency employees except those excused due to

 disability

 qualifying medical condition

 other compelling reason certified by the agency head and employees supervisor

 military spouses working remotely under the military spouse employment act



 submission process

i work in contract management and theres a legal concept called within the four corners of the contractmeaning only what is explicitly written in an agreement is enforceable this deferred resignation agreement offers no real guarantees beyond exempting the employee from the return to office rto mandate

 major concerns with this agreement

1 no legal funding commitment  under a continuing resolution cr the government cannot obligate funds beyond whats appropriated if opm lacks budget authority this agreement could be null and void under the antideficiency act ada

2 no mutual obligation illusory promise  the employee is locked into resigning but the government reserves the right to adjust revoke or deny benefits based on funding availability this makes it onesided and potentially unenforceable

3 no explicit severance or compensation  unlike voluntary early retirement vera or buyout programs vsip this offers no financial incentives or guaranteed payouts employees could resign and receive nothing beyond what they were already entitled to

4 atwill employment still applies  the government doesnt need this agreement to separate employees if funding is cut employees could still face reductions in force rifs or reassignments without this resignation letter

5 risk of government shutdown or budget issues  if funding isnt secured before the resignation date employees could lose expected benefits with no legal recourse

bottom line
this agreement provides no enforceable protections no guaranteed payouts and no obligation on the governments part employees signing this take all the risk while the agency retains discretion

the federal labor relations authority flra case between the national treasury employees union nteu and the federal deposit insurance corporation fdic case no 0ar5904 provides insight into how a union might fare in challenging a governmentmandated full return to office with no telework options  

case summary
		background during the covid19 pandemic the fdic expanded telework through a homebased option allowing employees to work primarily from home later the fdic required all employees to report to their official duty station at least once per pay period the nteu grieved alleging this directive violated their collective bargaining agreement cba
		arbitrators findings the arbitrator concluded that the union did not prove the fdic violated the cba additionally it was determined that provisions dictating telework frequency affect managements rights to direct employees and assign work under  7106 of the federal service labormanagement relations statute

implications for a full returntooffice mandate
	1	management rights the flra has upheld that management possesses the authority to direct employees and assign work which includes determining telework policies a mandate requiring a full return to the office aligns with these rights
	2	collective bargaining agreements while management holds these rights agencies must still negotiate the impact and implementation of such decisions with unions this means that while the decision to end telework may not be negotiable the procedures for its implementation and addressing employees concerns are subject to bargaining
	3	unfair labor practices ulp if an agency unilaterally enforces a full returntooffice policy without engaging in required negotiations over its impact and implementation it could be committing a ulp

conclusion

based on the nteu vs fdic case while a union may not successfully challenge the decision to mandate a full return to the office due to managements established rights it can contest the manner in which the policy is implemented if an agency fails to negotiate the impact and implementation details with the union the union could prevail in a ulp claim therefore while the overarching policy may stand unions have a pathway to influence its execution to protect employees interests

employees and their unions could launch several legal challenges against this opm guidance and the underlying presidential memorandum focusing on both procedural and substantive grounds  heres a breakdown

challenges to the presidential memorandum limiting lameduck cbas

  ultra vireslack of statutory authority  a primary challenge would be that the president exceeded his authority  while the president has some management authority over federal agencies this memo arguably attempts to dictate terms of collective bargaining a process governed by the federal service labormanagement relations statute fslmrs  the argument would be that the memo impermissibly interferes with the fslmrss carefully constructed framework  the policy and purpose section of the memo which claims that such agreements run counter to americas system of democratic selfgovernment and inhibit the presidents authority is a political argument not a legal one the memo needs grounding in existing law

  violation of the fslmrs the memos attempt to invalidate portions of existing cbas or prevent future cbas within a specific timeframe could be seen as a direct violation of the fslmrs which guarantees federal employees the right to bargain collectively  unions could argue that the memo impermissibly interferes with this right and undermines the collective bargaining process

  arbitrary and capricious  the 30day timeframe could be challenged as arbitrary and capricious lacking a rational basis  why 30 days  what evidence supports this specific timeframe as necessary to protect the incoming administrations policy prerogatives  a court might find the justification insufficient

  procedural issues if applicable  depending on how the memo was issued there might be procedural challenges related to notice and comment or other administrative law requirements  however presidential memoranda often have less stringent procedural requirements than formal regulations

  first amendment concerns potentially while less likely to succeed a creative argument might be that the memo infringes on the first amendment rights of federal employees and unions to associate and bargain collectively
challenges to the opm guidance

  reliance on a flawed presidential memorandum  because the opm guidance is based on the presidential memorandum any successful challenge to the memo would likely invalidate the guidance as well

  misinterpretation of flra precedent  the guidances interpretation of flra precedent regarding management rights and the scope of bargaining could be challenged  unions might argue that the opm is overstating managements rights and understating the scope of negotiable issues especially concerning telework  the cases cited may not support the broad assertions made in the memo

  failure to bargain in good faith  the guidance suggests that agencies can declare cba provisions unenforceable and implement changes before bargaining  this could be challenged as a violation of the duty to bargain in good faith under the fslmrs  while postimplementation bargaining is mentioned the timing and context are crucial  unions will argue that meaningful bargaining must occur before changes are implemented

  impact on employee morale and productivity  while not strictly a legal challenge unions could highlight the potential negative impact of the guidance on employee morale productivity and recruitmentretention  this could be used to pressure the agency and the administration to reconsider the guidance

specific examples related to telework
  substantive amount of telework as a management right  the claim that the substantive amount of telework is solely a management right is a key point of contention  unions would argue that the impact of telework policies on working conditions is negotiable even if the ultimate decision on telework levels rests with management

  retroactive application to existing cbas  the guidances attempt to invalidate existing cba provisions related to telework is a major point of vulnerability  unions will argue that the government is attempting to unilaterally rewrite contracts which is generally not permissible

important considerations
  political context  these challenges would likely play out in a highly politicized environment  the administrations stance on federal employee unions and collective bargaining would be a significant factor

  flra deference  the courts often defer to the flras expertise in interpreting the fslmrs  therefore the flras position on these issues would be crucial

  injunctive relief  unions might seek injunctive relief to prevent the implementation of the opm guidance and the presidential memorandum while the legal challenges are pending

in short this opm guidance and the underlying presidential memorandum are highly vulnerable to legal challenges  employees and their unions have several strong arguments based on statutory interpretation administrative law and potentially even constitutional principles  the success of these challenges will depend on the specific facts of each case the prevailing legal precedent and the political climate
